name: Anglo-American University
summary: Private English-language university in central Prague, founded 1990; 7 three-year BA majors with US and Czech accreditation and rolling admission.

ib.text: IB Diploma with at least 24 points and CAS, TOK and EE passed. It waives the English test and is recognised without nostrification; a personal statement and an interview decide.

noDeadline: Rolling admission all year; apply early for autumn 2027

apply.via: AAU application portal or Common App

programmes.name: Psychology
programmes.about: Foundations of psychology and mental health practice, aimed at work in psychological counselling, personal development and well-being; ends with a thesis defence and an oral state exam.
programmes.overview: You cover the main branches of psychology, from developmental, personality, social and biological psychology to counselling and industrial/organizational psychology, alongside research methods, statistics, assessment and ethics. Electives reach into areas such as abnormal, cognitive, positive, traffic and political psychology. Practical, experiential learning is built in, and every student completes an internship, a thesis seminar and a thesis defence. Graduates take assistant roles in clinics, counselling centres, HR, research and social services, or continue to a master's in psychology.
programmes.selectionNote: Rolling: personal statement (250–650 words), CV and transcript, then an interview with the Dean's Office. It filled up for 2026/27, so apply early.

programmes.name: International and European Legal Studies
programmes.about: How international and EU law shape business, diplomacy and society, with internships, small classes and mentoring from international faculty.
programmes.overview: The core courses cover public international law, European Union law, international business law and transactions, comparative constitutional law, human rights in the EU, international criminal law and the law of international organizations, with seven electives such as environmental, intellectual property or commercial law. Classes are small, and teaching mixes case studies, moot court competitions and a thesis seminar on legal research. Internships are offered at law firms and consultancies, and Prague's embassies and international bodies add contacts. Graduates work as legal advisors, compliance specialists, NGO officers, researchers or diplomats.
programmes.selectionNote: Rolling: personal statement (250–650 words), CV and transcript, then an interview with the Dean's Office; the decision comes a week later.

programmes.name: International Relations
programmes.about: International relations theory, global and domestic politics and philosophy, with an internship and thesis. Take the major or a concentration in Global Security Studies, International Law or Human Rights.
programmes.overview: You study politics, political philosophy, international organizations, nationalism, the Cold War, global power politics, global security and political economy, plus research methods, and choose electives on topics such as human rights, migration, energy security or the politics of regions like Asia, Africa and China. A compulsory internship places students at embassies, ministries, think tanks and NGOs, and the degree ends with a thesis. Clubs such as Model UN and Diplomacy sit alongside classes, and optional minors broaden the major. Graduates go into diplomacy, public service, research and humanitarian work.
programmes.selectionNote: Rolling: personal statement (250–650 words), CV and transcript, then an interview with the Dean's Office; the decision comes a week later.

programmes.name: Business Administration
programmes.about: Management, marketing, finance, economics and leadership with internships. Take the major or a concentration: marketing and digital communications, entrepreneurship, global management, data analytics, or accounting, finance and ESG.
programmes.overview: You study financial accounting, corporate finance, management, marketing, business mathematics and statistics, and digital skills and AI for business, with general education in economics, law and history. Teaching leans on practical projects in small international teams and a required internship; the degree closes with a thesis seminar on business research and a defence. The major has no fixed concentrations, so electives and seven business courses of your choice shape it, and minors in other fields are possible. Graduates become management trainees, analysts, marketers, financial analysts, consultants or entrepreneurs.
programmes.selectionNote: Rolling: personal statement (250–650 words), CV and transcript, then an interview with the Dean's Office; the decision comes a week later.

programmes.name: Humanities, Society and Culture
programmes.about: Philosophy, literature, history and the arts and how they shape society, with an internship and thesis. Take the major or a concentration in sociology and leadership, language and culture, or creative writing.
programmes.overview: The degree draws on philosophy, cultural anthropology, history, the arts, literature and film studies, together with social theory and research methods. Teaching is in small seminars with close contact with international faculty. A required internship places students at schools, museums and archives, media outlets and NGOs, and a final independent thesis is supervised by faculty. Extended major groups let you focus on philosophy, arts and media, history and culture, or literature. Graduates move into cultural management, publishing, media, education, social research and nonprofit work, or on to graduate study.
programmes.selectionNote: Rolling: personal statement (250–650 words), CV and transcript, then an interview with the Dean's Office; the decision comes a week later.

programmes.name: Journalism and Media Studies
programmes.about: Journalism combined with media studies, film studies, marketing and public relations, with an internship; a Public Relations and Marketing concentration is offered.
programmes.overview: You combine reporting, media theory, digital media, visual journalism, film and marketing with foundation courses in history, politics, sociology and psychology. Hands-on work includes the student magazine Lennon Wall, internet radio through Soundbricks, and articles produced with Radio Prague International. A compulsory internship has placed students with Radio Free Europe and Czech News Center, and a thesis closes the degree. Extended major courses let you lean toward writing, media studies, film, photography or digital media. Graduates work in print and web media, publishing, cultural management and nonprofit organizations.
programmes.selectionNote: Rolling: personal statement (250–650 words), CV and transcript, then an interview with the Dean's Office; the decision comes a week later.

programmes.name: Visual Art Studies
programmes.about: Art history, curatorial studies and studio art together, giving a grounding in both the theory and the practice of the visual arts in Prague.
programmes.overview: The programme rests on art history, curatorial studies and studio practice, with courses from classical to contemporary art, critical theory and visual literacy. Studio classes in drawing, painting and cross-media work run from foundation to advanced level, and student work is exhibited. Internships at institutions such as Kunsthalle Prague, DOX and MeetFactory are mandatory, and you write an independent thesis. Electives fall into making art, art and media, and art, culture and the market. Graduates become curators, artists, designers, photographers, art dealers or arts managers, or continue to graduate study.
programmes.selectionNote: Rolling: personal statement (250–650 words), CV and transcript, then an interview with the Dean's Office; the decision comes a week later.

notes: Fees are set in Czech crowns per semester (EU/EFTA rate CZK 125,489 in 2026/27); AAU expects a 5% rise for new students, so check the price for 2027 entry.
The IB Diploma is on AAU's list of diplomas recognised automatically under Czech law; bring certified copies of your diploma before classes start.
You can start in autumn or spring; the application fee is CZK 1,000 and is not refunded.
